quotes.verbatim_quote: Close Block Voicings in which the notes are packed closely together.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines close block voicings as a fundamental vertical harmony structure.

quotes.verbatim_quote: Open Voicings in which the notes are spread apart.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines open voicings as the second primary vertical structure.

quotes.verbatim_quote: Closed voiced chords can be opened up as far as your reach will permit, simply by moving one or more chordal tones up or down an octave.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Prescribes the technique for converting close voicings to open voicings.

quotes.topic: Voice leading is primary connective force
quotes.verbatim_quote: The melody lines formed by each of the chordal tones is the most important single factor linking one chord to another. In four part harmony, for example, one is really dealing with four separate melody lines.
quotes.why_load_bearing: States the foundational principle that voice leading is the primary connective force in harmony.

quotes.verbatim_quote: PARALLEL MOTION, a chord progression in which each tone is moving the same number of scale steps and in the same direction.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Provides the formal definition of parallel motion.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
CONTRARY MOTION is, as the word im

Ex plies, a situation in which the chordal tones are
moving in opposite directions.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Provides the formal definition of contrary motion.

quotes.verbatim_quote: COUNTER LINES are usually treated as a melodic accompaniment to the main body of a tune. They are also used as connecting lines from one chord to another and, on guitar, are frequently found in the second voice from the top. When the main melody has little motion, the counter line can be more active.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines counter lines, prescribes their typical placement on guitar (second voice from top), and gives the rule for activity level.

quotes.verbatim_quote: A COMMON TONE is a note that is related to, and sustained through, a sequence of chords played in succession.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Provides the formal definition of the common tone device.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
BLOCK CHORDS. Here is a rudimentary. yet effective way of producing melody and
harmony simultaneously. This is done by placing a full chord underneath each melody note. The chords can
be either close or open voicings.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines block chords and prescribes placing a full chord under each melody note.

quotes.verbatim_quote: You might experiment with picking techniques here: For example, all down strokes, or alternate down and up strokes, or plucking all strings simultaneously with fingers.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Prescribes specific picking/plucking technique options for executing block chords.

quotes.verbatim_quote: Note: The Gm7 in bar 3 is being used as a substitute for Eb maj 9.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Prescribes a specific chord substitution (Gm7 for Eb maj9) in context.

quotes.topic: Block chord effect: voicing must move with melody
quotes.verbatim_quote:
The block chord effect is best achieved when the chordal tones are made to move when the melody moves.
and preferably in the same direction as the melody. Often the melody can be fingered easily without having
to change the chord form, but this tends to destroy the block chord effect; therefore it is more desirable to
change the voicing or inversion with each new melody note, in order to create the effect of all lines moving
at once.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Gives the rule for achieving block chord effect: change voicing/inversion with each melody note.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
SUSTAINED CHORD BACKGROUND is a modification of the block chord style. in that
one chord is sustained through two or more melody notes.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines sustained chord background and its relationship to block chords.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
When a chord is sustained throughout a long sequence of melody notes, fingering requirements frequent
make it necessary to drop one or more of the chordal tones in order to manipulate the melody. This
especially true in improvising with the aforementioned common guitar voicings when the voice leadi
not been fully worked out. However, if each chordal tone is sustained for as long as possible, the listenc
usually remember those notes that have been dropped.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Explains practical rule for handling dropped chord tones, relying on listener's harmonic memory.

quotes.topic: Short chord punctuations and harmonic continuity
quotes.verbatim_quote:
SHORT CHORD PUNCTUATIONS., Because of the listener’s ability to remember the soun
of harmony, it is possible to outline the flow of harmony by short chord punctuations. These can be use
without sacrificing harmonic continuity, when they are played with authority and appropriately placed withi:
the bar. This continuity can be further reinforced by choosing melodies which emphasize chordal tones.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines short chord punctuations and gives the rule for maintaining harmonic continuity.
